extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / graduate students in real analysis / measure theory
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted chapter material on convolution, translations, approximate identities, properties of Borel measures on open/compact sets, relationship between Riemann and Lebesgue integrals, change-of-variables, gamma function and Sard's theorem. The page gives precise hypotheses and conclusions (propositions/theorems), sketches of proofs, examples (polar coordinates, Gaussian integral), and remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.13 — Commutativity and associativity of convolution
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonnegative Borel functions on R^N, convolution is commutative and associative (formulas of the form (f * g) * h = f * (g * h) and f * g = g * f hold when the integrals are defined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Fubini's Theorem and Theorem 6.10; change-of-variable manipulations are used to justify equalities. Notes explain how to extend to real- or complex-valued functions by decomposing into nonnegative parts and adjusting on null sets so that associativity/commutativity remain valid even when functions can take sign or complex values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.14 — Cases where convolution is finite a.e. and norm inequalities (Young-type inequalities)
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonnegative Borel functions f and g on R^N, convolution f * g is finite almost everywhere in listed cases and the indicated norm inequalities hold: (a) f ∈ L^1 and g ∈ L^1 ⇒ f * g defined a.e. and ||f * g||_1 ≤ ||f||_1 ||g||_1; (b) f ∈ L^1, g ∈ L^2 (or vice versa) ⇒ f * g ∈ L^2 and ||f * g||_2 ≤ ||f||_1 ||g||_2; (c) f ∈ L^1, g ∈ L^∞ (or vice versa) ⇒ f * g ∈ L^∞ and ||f * g||_∞ ≤ ||f||_1 ||g||_∞; (d) f, g ∈ L^2 ⇒ f * g is (everywhere defined and) bounded and ||f * g||_∞ ≤ ||f||_2 ||g||_2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use Minkowski's inequality for integrals, translation invariance of Lebesgue measure, and Schwarz inequality for the L^2 case. Remarks indicate these estimates remain valid even if scalar-valued functions are not necessarily nonnegative provided definitions are adjusted on null sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.15 — Convolution commutes with translations
rubrics_metrics.description: For functions f and g (in the appropriate spaces so convolutions make sense), the translation operator commutes with convolution: τ_t(f * g) = (τ_t f) * g = f * (τ_t g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses translation invariance of Lebesgue measure; compute both sides and use change of variable y ↦ y - t. Statement is given for the standard translation operator τ_t.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.16 — Continuity of translations in L^p (1 ≤ p < ∞)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ L^p(R^N) with 1 ≤ p < ∞, then translations are continuous in the L^p norm: lim_{h→0} ||τ_h f - f||_p = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: use density of C_c(R^N) in L^p (Corollary 6.4a) together with dominated convergence for compactly supported continuous approximants. Remark: continuity fails in L^∞, and a substitute result is discussed later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 6.17 — Approximation of convolutions by finite linear combinations of translates
rubrics_metrics.description: Let 1 ≤ p < ∞ and let g_1,...,g_r be finitely many functions in L^p(R^N). For any ε>0 and any f ∈ L^1(R^N), there exist finitely many points y_j ∈ R^N and constants c_j such that for each k (1≤k≤r) the L^p-distance || f * g_k - Σ_j c_j τ_{y_j} g_k ||_p ≤ ε (with a uniform finite number of terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs V = set of L^1 functions f for which such approximation is possible for every ε, shows indicator functions of compact sets lie in V (use Prop.6.16 and uniform continuity of translates of g_k), and closes V under linear combinations and limits using density arguments. Remark: this yields that convolutions f * g can be approximated by finite combinations of translates of g.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.18 — Convolution yields bounded uniformly continuous functions in certain pairings
rubrics_metrics.description: In R^N with Lebesgue measure, the convolution of L^1 with L^∞ (or L^∞ with L^1) or L^2 with L^2 produces an everywhere-defined bounded uniformly continuous function. Moreover, the indicated sup-norm bounds hold, e.g. ||f * g||_∞ ≤ ||f||_1 ||g||_∞ (and similar inequalities in the other cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the integral representation, the bound from Hölder/Young/Schwarz inequalities, and Prop.6.15 and 6.16 to show uniform continuity by controlling ||(f* g)(·+h) - (f* g)(·)||_∞ via translation continuity in L^p. The result strengthens mere L^∞ membership to an everywhere defined uniformly continuous representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 6.19 — Differentiation under convolution (regularity transfer)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is compactly supported and of class C^n (n≥1) on R^N and g ∈ L^p(R^N) with p ∈ {1,2,∞} (appropriate cases), then f * g is of class C^n and D^α(f * g) = (D^α f) * g for each multi-index α with |α| ≤ n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: use translation invariance, approximation by difference quotients and dominated convergence; first show for first derivatives and iterate. Compact support of f ensures uniform convergence of mollified derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 6.20 — Dilation approximate identity and its convergence properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Let φ ∈ L^1(R^N) and define φ_ε(x) = ε^{-N} φ(ε^{-1} x). Put c = ∫_{R^N} φ. Then: (a) for 1 ≤ p < ∞ (and p=1 or p=2 in text), if f ∈ L^p then ||φ_ε * f - c f||_p → 0 as ε → 0; (b) analogous convergence statements for other p as stated; (c) if f is bounded and continuous at x, then (φ_ε * f)(x) → c f(x); (d) convergence in (c) is uniform on sets where f is uniformly continuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Minkowski's inequality for integrals, translation continuity (Prop.6.16), and dominated convergence. Remarks: this gives the classical approximate identity / mollifier behavior: convolution with concentrated dilates approximates scaling of the identity operator; special cases produce mollification and density/approximation results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 6.21 — Adjusting L^∞ functions to uniformly continuous representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ L^∞(R^N) satisfies lim_{t→0} ||τ_t f - f||_∞ = 0 (continuity in sup-norm under translations), then f can be modified on a set of measure zero to become uniformly continuous (i.e., there exists a uniformly continuous bounded g equal to f a.e.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a compactly supported C_c approximate identity φ_ε and Theorem 6.20 to obtain uniformly continuous approximants φ_{ε_n} * f that are Cauchy in sup-norm and converge uniformly to a uniformly continuous limit g which differs from f only on a null set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 6.22 — Exhaustion and approximation on open sets V
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) There exists a sequence {F_n} of compact subsets with F_n ⊆ F_{n+1} and ∪_n F_n = V where F_n ⊆ interior(F_{n+1}); (b) For any compact K⊆V there exists a decreasing sequence of open sets U_n with compact closure in V and ∩_n U_n = K; (c) For any compact K⊆V there exists a decreasing sequence of functions in C_c(V) with values in [0,1] with pointwise limit equal to the indicator of K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive proofs use distance-to-complement functions and standard Urysohn-type constructions; these lemmas are used to extend regularity and density arguments from R^N to arbitrary open V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.23 — Description of Borel σ-algebra on open sets
rubrics_metrics.description: For a nonempty open V⊆R^N, BN(V) (Borel sets relative to V) is the smallest σ-algebra on V containing the open sets of V, and equivalently the smallest σ-algebra containing the compact subsets of V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof applies Lemma 6.24 and the exhaustion by compact sets from Lemma 6.22a; this justifies working with BN(V) as the natural σ-algebra for Borel measurability on open sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 6.25 — Regularity of Borel measures on open sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Borel measure µ on an open set V⊆R^N is regular: for any Borel E⊆V, µ(E) = sup {µ(K): K⊆E, K compact in V} = inf {µ(U): U⊇E, U open in V}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof follows the same pattern as regularity on R^N by applying Lemma 6.22 parts (a),(b). Remark: if µ is extended by zero outside V to R^N one obtains a Borel measure on R^N that may fail finiteness on compacts; nevertheless regularity on V holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 6.26 — Uniqueness of Borel measures via integrals of C_c functions
rubrics_metrics.description: If µ and ν are Borel measures on open V and ∫_V f dµ = ∫_V f dν for every f ∈ C_c(V), then µ = ν.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from Theorem 6.25 and approximation of indicators by C_c functions (Lemma 6.22c). Standard uniqueness-by-duality result for regular Borel measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 6.27 — Density/separability results for C_c and L^p on open sets
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) C_c(V) is dense in L^p(V, µ) for 1 ≤ p < ∞; (b) the smallest closed subspace of L^p(V, µ) containing all indicator functions of compact subsets of V is the whole L^p(V, µ); (c) C_c(V) under supremum norm is separable; (d) L^p(V, µ) is separable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use Lemma 6.22c to approximate indicators by continuous compactly supported functions and standard density arguments (Propositions 5.55/5.56 cited). Separability is obtained by covering V by a countable union of relatively compact open sets and taking countable dense subsets on each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.28 — Measurable preimages under continuous/Borel maps
rubrics_metrics.description: If F: V → V_0 is continuous (or even Borel measurable), then for every E ∈ BN(V_0), the preimage F^{-1}(E) ∈ BN(V). Equivalently, continuous maps carry Borel sets back to Borel sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observes that the class of sets whose preimage is Borel is a σ-algebra containing basic geometric rectangles; same argument as for R^N. Corollary: homeomorphisms carry BN(V) to BN(V_0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.30 — Regularity of Borel measures on compact sets
rubrics_metrics.description: If K is a nonempty compact subset of R^N and µ a Borel measure on K, then µ is regular: for E Borel in K, µ(E) = sup{µ(K0): K0⊆E, K0 compact in K} = inf{µ(U): U⊇E, U relatively open in K}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows by extending µ to a Borel measure on R^N (zero off K) and applying regularity on R^N; no separate argument is needed because µ(K) < ∞.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 6.31 — Equivalence of Riemann integrability and continuity almost everywhere
rubrics_metrics.description: A bounded real-valued function f on a compact geometric rectangle A⊆R^N is Riemann integrable iff f is continuous except on a Lebesgue measurable set of measure zero. In this case f is Lebesgue measurable and the Riemann and Lebesgue integrals agree: ∫_A f dx (Riemann) = ∫_A f dx (Lebesgue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Riemann upper and lower sums and constructs Borel functions L_k and U_k from partition extrema; uses dominated convergence and the fact that the set where lower and upper limits differ has measure 0. This yields measurability and equality of integrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 6.32 — Change-of-variables formula (C^1 diffeomorphism)
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ: U → φ(U) is a C^1 one-to-one map from open U⊆R^N onto open φ(U)⊆R^N with det φ'(x) nowhere zero, then for every nonnegative Borel function f on φ(U), ∫_{φ(U)} f(y) dy = ∫_U f(φ(x)) |det φ'(x)| dx.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: start from the change-of-variables identity for C_c functions (Theorem 3.34), view integrands as continuous on R^N by extension by zero, reinterpret as Lebesgue integrals (Prop.6.11 or Thm.6.31), and extend to nonnegative Borel functions using measure pushforward and uniqueness (Cor.6.26). Remarks discuss σ-algebras on φ(U) and practical examples (polar coordinates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application — Polar coordinates example
rubrics_metrics.description: In R^2 the polar map φ(r,θ) = (r cosθ, r sinθ) (0<r<∞, 0<θ<2π) has Jacobian r, and the change-of-variables yields ∫_{R^2} f(x,y) dx dy = ∫_{0}^{∞} ∫_{0}^{2π} f(r cosθ, r sinθ) r dθ dr for nonnegative Borel f. Exceptional low-dimensional subsets omitted by φ have measure zero and do not affect integrals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as sample application (Gaussian integral calculation) and to illustrate handling of exceptional sets of measure zero when φ(U) does not cover the whole target region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.33 — Gaussian integral evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The one-dimensional Gaussian integral satisfies ∫_{-∞}^{∞} e^{-π x^2} dx = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute square of the integral, convert to polar coordinates in R^2 and evaluate radial integral; used later for normalization in Fourier analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 6.34 — Basic properties of the gamma function
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs via integration by parts, iteration, and the Gaussian integral (Prop.6.33) for Γ(1/2). The text remarks on integrability of t^{s-1} e^{-t} and reduction to real s>0 for integrability verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 6.35 — Sard's Theorem (critical values have measure zero)
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ: V → R^N is a smooth map on open V⊆R^N, then the set of critical values (images of points where the derivative has rank < N) is a Borel set of Lebesgue measure zero in R^N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch: the set where the derivative has rank ≤ N-1 is relatively closed and is a countable union of compacts; the set of critical values is the union of compact images and is Borel. The proof reduces to compact geometric rectangles and uses further local analysis (continuation beyond chunk). Sard's theorem is presented as giving a general statement that 'lower-dimensional' images have measure zero and is used to justify that exceptions in change-of-variables often occupy sets of measure zero.
